decisions.reason: As a close variant of the core cardboard display range, it is cheap for this large firm to carry and still offers option value while market acceptance remains uncertain.
This pegboard-backed display is still near the established offer, so management would likely keep it as a low-cost experiment unless clearer weak demand emerges.
A standard quarter-pallet cardboard display fits the firm's existing capabilities very well, making the downside of keeping it low and the option value relatively high.
The eighth-pallet format is another adjacent catalogue variant that can be supported with existing design and production assets, so it is likely to be retained for now.

Because the wooden pallet display is somewhat farther from the paper-based core it has a higher chance of being culled, but management would still likely keep it one more year while its potential is unresolved.
Although the media-products niche may be more specialized, this quarter-pallet cardboard display remains close enough to the core business that keeping it preserves useful upside at limited cost.
